---
title: "Case study: cosponsorship in the 118th Congress"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6,
                      warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(amorem)
source("case-helpers.R")
source("anim.R")
party_col <- c(D = "#4F8CC9", R = "#C8729A", I = "#9AA0A6")
party_name <- c(D = "Democrat", R = "Republican", I = "Independent")
# heat_adjacency() and forest() of case-helpers.R, with room for a title above the plot
heat_titled <- function(mat, groups, colours, col_hi = "#178E8E") {
  n <- nrow(mat); v <- log1p(mat)
  par(mar = c(1, 1.4, 3.6, 1))
  ramp <- grDevices::colorRampPalette(c("#FFFFFF", alpha(col_hi, 0.35), col_hi, "#0B4F4F"))(64)
  image(seq_len(n), seq_len(n), t(v[n:1, ]), col = ramp, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", useRaster = TRUE)
  cut <- which(head(groups, -1) != tail(groups, -1)) + 0.5
  abline(v = cut, h = n + 1 - cut, col = ink_soft, lwd = 0.6)
  rect(-0.02 * n, n:1 - 0.5, 0.005 * n, n:1 + 0.5, col = colours[as.character(groups)], border = NA, xpd = TRUE)
}
forest_titled <- function(est, se, labels, col = pal[1]) {
  k <- length(est); y <- k:1; lo <- est - 1.96 * se; hi <- est + 1.96 * se
  par(mar = c(3.4, max(nchar(labels)) * 0.42 + 1, 3.2, 1))
  plot(est, y, xlim = range(c(lo, hi, 0)), ylim = c(0.5, k + 0.5), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", type = "n")
  abline(v = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
  segments(lo, y, hi, y, col = col, lwd = 2.2)
  points(est, y, pch = 21, bg = "white", col = col, cex = 1.3, lwd = 1.6)
  axis(1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)
  mtext("effect on the log-rate", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
}

# draw_hypergraph() of case-helpers.R with each cosponsor line in the cosponsor's colour
hypergraph_coloured <- function(hl, member_col, member_label = NULL, seed = 1) {
  ev <- paste0("e", seq_len(nrow(hl)))
  eI <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(hl)), function(k) data.frame(from = hl$I[[k]], to = ev[k], side = "I")))
  eJ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(hl)), function(k) if (length(hl$J[[k]])) data.frame(from = hl$J[[k]], to = ev[k], side = "J")))
  e <- rbind(eI, eJ); e$w <- 1
  actors <- unique(c(eI$from, eJ$from))
  lay <- layout_graph(e, ids = c(actors, ev), seed = seed); xy <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(lay)), lay$id)
  plot(NA, xlim = c(-0.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-0.05, max(lay$y) + 0.05), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1)
  segments(lay$x[xy[e$from]], lay$y[xy[e$from]], lay$x[xy[e$to]], lay$y[xy[e$to]],
           col = alpha(member_col[e$from], ifelse(e$side == "I", 0.9, 0.38)), lwd = ifelse(e$side == "I", 2, 0.7))
  deg <- table(e$from); a <- lay[lay$id %in% actors, ]
  cex <- 0.5 + 1.9 * sqrt(as.numeric(deg[a$id]) / max(deg))
  points(a$x, a$y, pch = 21, bg = member_col[a$id], col = "white", cex = cex, lwd = 0.7)
  sq <- lay[lay$id %in% ev, ]
  points(sq$x, sq$y, pch = 22, bg = "white", col = "#4A5560", cex = 0.75, lwd = 1.1)
  if (!is.null(member_label)) { k <- which(a$id %in% names(member_label))
    .repel_labels(a$x[k], a$y[k], member_label[a$id[k]], 0.009 * cex[k], 0.55) }
}
# chord() of case-helpers.R with chosen ribbons emphasised and labelled; others faded
chord_emph <- function(mat, colours, emph, emph_lab, gap = 0.03, label_cex = 0.72) {
  g <- rownames(mat); n <- length(g); tot <- rowSums(mat) + colSums(mat)
  plot(NA, xlim = c(-1.35, 1.35), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.3), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", asp = 1)
  span <- 2 * pi - n * gap; w <- span * tot / sum(tot)
  start <- cumsum(c(0, head(w + gap, -1))) + pi / 2
  arc <- function(a0, a1, r = 1, k = 40) { s <- seq(a0, a1, length.out = k); cbind(r * cos(s), r * sin(s)) }
  out_pos <- start; in_pos <- start + w * rowSums(mat) / tot; scale <- w / tot
  pull <- function(q) { s <- seq(0, 1, length.out = length(q$x)); f <- 1 - 0.85 * sin(pi * s); list(x = q$x * f, y = q$y * f) }
  rib <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) for (j in seq_len(n)) {
    v <- mat[i, j]; if (v <= 0) next
    a0 <- out_pos[i]; a1 <- a0 + v * scale[i]; out_pos[i] <- a1
    b0 <- in_pos[j]; b1 <- b0 + v * scale[j]; in_pos[j] <- b1
    p1 <- arc(a0, a1, 0.96); p2 <- arc(b0, b1, 0.96)
    q1 <- pull(.bezier(p1[nrow(p1), 1], p1[nrow(p1), 2], p2[1, 1], p2[1, 2], 0, 30))
    q2 <- pull(.bezier(p2[nrow(p2), 1], p2[nrow(p2), 2], p1[1, 1], p1[1, 2], 0, 30))
    rib[[length(rib) + 1]] <- list(i = i, j = j, x = c(p1[, 1], q1$x, p2[, 1], q2$x), y = c(p1[, 2], q1$y, p2[, 2], q2$y),
                                   mx = mean(c(q1$x[9], q2$x[22])), my = mean(c(q1$y[9], q2$y[22])))
  }
  on_top <- vapply(rib, function(r) emph[r$i, r$j], TRUE)
  for (r in c(rib[!on_top], rib[on_top])) {
    e <- emph[r$i, r$j]
    polygon(r$x, r$y, col = alpha(colours[g[r$i]], if (e) 0.85 else 0.16),
            border = alpha(colours[g[r$i]], if (e) 1 else 0.3), lwd = 0.5)
  }
  marks <- lapply(rib[on_top], function(r) c(x = r$mx, y = r$my, lab = emph_lab[r$i, r$j]))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    p <- arc(start[i], start[i] + w[i], 1); q <- arc(start[i] + w[i], start[i], 1.06)
    polygon(c(p[, 1], q[, 1]), c(p[, 2], q[, 2]), col = colours[g[i]], border = NA)
    m <- start[i] + w[i] / 2
    text(1.17 * cos(m), 1.17 * sin(m), g[i], cex = label_cex, col = ink,
         adj = c(ifelse(cos(m) < -0.2, 1, ifelse(cos(m) > 0.2, 0, 0.5)), 0.5), xpd = TRUE)
  }
  for (mk in marks) { x <- as.numeric(mk["x"]); y <- as.numeric(mk["y"])
    w <- strwidth(mk["lab"], cex = 0.68, font = 2); h <- strheight(mk["lab"], cex = 0.68, font = 2)
    rect(x - w / 2 - 0.03, y - h / 2 - 0.03, x + w / 2 + 0.03, y + h / 2 + 0.03, col = alpha("white", 0.85), border = NA)
    text(x, y, mk["lab"], cex = 0.68, col = ink, font = 2, xpd = TRUE) }
}
```

# Case study: cosponsorship in the 118th Congress

A bill in the US Congress has one sponsor and any number of cosponsors who
sign on to it. Each bill is therefore a directed hyperevent: a sender `I` (the
sponsor) and a receiver set `J` (the cosponsors) at a time `t` (the day it is
introduced). `congress_bills_118` holds every House and Senate bill of the
118th Congress (3 January 2023 to 3 January 2025) in that form, and
`congress_members_118` gives each member's party and state.

```{r data}
data(congress_bills_118)
data(congress_members_118)
cb <- congress_bills_118
m  <- congress_members_118
party <- setNames(m$party, m$bioguide_id)
state <- setNames(m$state, m$bioguide_id)
short <- setNames(paste0(sub(",.*", "", sub("^(Rep|Sen|Del|Resc)\\. ", "", m$name)),
                         " (", m$party, "-", m$state, ")"), m$bioguide_id)
chamber <- ifelse(grepl("^s", cb$bill), "Senate", "House")
sponsor <- vapply(cb$I, `[`, "", 1)
size <- lengths(cb$J)
c(bills = nrow(cb), house = sum(chamber == "House"), senate = sum(chamber == "Senate"),
  members = nrow(m), with_cosponsors = sum(size > 0), median_cosponsors = median(size))
```

```{r numbers, include = FALSE}
flows <- data.frame(s = rep(sponsor, size), j = unlist(cb$J), ch = rep(chamber, size))
flows$sp <- party[flows$s]; flows$jp <- party[flows$j]
cross <- mean(flows$sp != flows$jp, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## One day of bills as a hypergraph

```{r hypergraph, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7.4, fig.alt = "Senate bills of one day drawn as a hypergraph: bills are squares joined to their sponsor and cosponsors"}
day_s <- cb[chamber == "Senate" & size > 0, ]
busiest <- names(which.max(table(day_s$date)))
h <- day_s[day_s$date == as.Date(busiest), ]
h <- h[order(-lengths(h$J)), ][seq_len(min(18, nrow(h))), ]
par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))
hypergraph_coloured(h, party_col[party[unique(unlist(c(h$I, h$J)))]] |>
                  setNames(unique(unlist(c(h$I, h$J)))),
                member_label = short[unique(unlist(h$I))])
title_left(sprintf("%d Senate bills introduced on %s", nrow(h), format(as.Date(busiest), "%d %B %Y")),
           "square: a bill; thick line to its sponsor (labelled); thin lines to its cosponsors, coloured by the cosponsor's party; dot size: bills joined that day")
legend_groups(setNames(party_col, party_name[names(party_col)]), "bottomright")
```

The bills of `r format(as.Date(busiest), "%d %B %Y")`, the day with most Senate
bills that have cosponsors, drawn as a hypergraph. A senator who cosponsors
several of these bills ties them together, and most bills draw their
cosponsors from the sponsor's own party.

## The two blocs and the members between them

```{r network-data}
pairs <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(flows))), flows[, c("s", "j")], sum)
names(pairs) <- c("from", "to", "w")
act <- table(c(flows$s, flows$j))
top <- names(sort(act, decreasing = TRUE))[1:150]
strong <- pairs[pairs$from %in% top & pairs$to %in% top & pairs$w >= 5, ]
g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(strong[, c("from", "to")], directed = FALSE)
main <- names(which(igraph::components(g)$membership == which.max(igraph::components(g)$csize)))
strong <- strong[strong$from %in% main & strong$to %in% main, ]
lay <- layout_graph(strong, ids = main, seed = 3)
# bridging: share of a member's cosponsorships that go to the other party's bills
as_cos <- flows[!is.na(flows$sp) & !is.na(flows$jp), ]
bridge <- tapply(as_cos$sp != as_cos$jp, as_cos$j, mean)
bridge_n <- table(as_cos$j)
```

```{r network, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5, fig.alt = "Network of the most active members: Democrats and Republicans form two clusters joined by a few bipartisan members"}
nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),
                    col = party_col[party[lay$id]], label = NA)
bridges <- names(sort(bridge[lay$id][bridge_n[lay$id] >= 50], decreasing = TRUE))[1:6]
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 3, 0.5))
draw_network(nodes, data.frame(from = strong$from, to = strong$to, w = strong$w,
                               col = party_col[party[strong$from]]),
             directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 2.4, ylim = c(-0.04, max(nodes$y) + 0.2))
# the bridging members: ringed, and labelled in a row above the graph with leader lines
b_ <- nodes[nodes$id %in% bridges, ]; b_ <- b_[order(b_$x), ]
points(b_$x, b_$y, pch = 21, bg = NA, col = ink, lwd = 2,
       cex = 0.6 + 2.6 * sqrt(b_$size / max(nodes$size)) + 0.35)
lx <- seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = nrow(b_)); ly <- max(nodes$y) + c(0.09, 0.16)[seq_len(nrow(b_)) %% 2 + 1]
segments(b_$x, b_$y, lx, ly - 0.012, col = ink, lwd = 0.7)
text(lx, ly, short[b_$id], cex = 0.62, col = ink, pos = 3, offset = 0.15)
title_left(sprintf("Cosponsorship among the %d most active members", nrow(lay)),
           "arrow: sponsor to a member who cosponsored at least 5 of their bills; ringed and labelled: the six members whose cosponsorships most often cross party lines")
legend_groups(setNames(party_col[c("D", "R")], party_name[c("D", "R")]), "bottomleft")
```

The layout separates the parties into two clusters. The labelled members are
those (among members with at least 50 cosponsorships) whose cosponsorships
most often go to the other party's bills; they sit between the clusters.
Across all bills, `r pct(cross)` of cosponsorships cross party lines.

## Flows between parties and chambers

```{r chord, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 7.5, fig.alt = "Chord diagram of cosponsorships between sponsor and cosponsor party in each chamber"}
lab <- function(ch, p) paste(ch, party_name[p])
fl <- flows[!is.na(flows$sp) & !is.na(flows$jp), ]
a <- lab(fl$ch, fl$sp); b <- lab(fl$ch, fl$jp)
lev <- c(lab("House", c("D", "R")), lab("Senate", c("D", "R", "I")))
M <- as.matrix(table(factor(a, lev), factor(b, lev)))
chord_col <- setNames(c("#4F8CC9", "#C8729A", "#2E6DA8", "#A84F79", "#9AA0A6"), lev)
hD <- lab("House", "D"); hR <- lab("House", "R")
emph <- matrix(FALSE, length(lev), length(lev), dimnames = list(lev, lev))
emph[hD, hR] <- emph[hR, hD] <- TRUE
elab <- matrix("", length(lev), length(lev), dimnames = list(lev, lev))
elab[hD, hR] <- sprintf("%s of cosponsors on House\nDemocratic bills are Republicans", pct(M[hD, hR] / sum(M[hD, ])))
elab[hR, hD] <- sprintf("%s of cosponsors on House\nRepublican bills are Democrats", pct(M[hR, hD] / sum(M[hR, ])))
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 3, 0.5))
chord_emph(M, chord_col, emph, elab)
title_left("Who cosponsors whose bills",
           "ribbon: from the sponsor's group to the cosponsors' group, width = cosponsorships; the two House cross-party ribbons are highlighted")
mtext(sprintf("%s of all cosponsorships stay within the sponsor's party and chamber (the faded ribbons that return to their own arc)",
              pct(sum(diag(M)) / sum(M))), side = 1, line = -0.6, cex = 0.68, col = ink_soft)
```

```{r chord-numbers, include = FALSE}
within <- sum(diag(M)) / sum(M)
hr <- M[lab("House", "R"), lab("House", "D")] / sum(M[lab("House", "R"), ])
hd <- M[lab("House", "D"), lab("House", "R")] / sum(M[lab("House", "D"), ])
```

`r pct(within)` of cosponsorships stay within the sponsor's party and chamber.
In the House, `r pct(hd)` of the cosponsorships on Democratic bills come from
Republicans and `r pct(hr)` of those on Republican bills come from Democrats.

## The House as an adjacency matrix

```{r heatmap, fig.width = 8.6, fig.height = 8.6, fig.alt = "Sponsor by cosponsor matrix of House members ordered by party and state: two dense diagonal blocks"}
hf <- flows[flows$ch == "House" & !is.na(flows$sp) & !is.na(flows$jp), ]
hm <- names(which(table(c(hf$s, hf$j)) >= 30))
ord <- hm[order(party[hm], state[hm], -as.numeric(table(c(hf$s, hf$j))[hm]))]
A <- matrix(0, length(ord), length(ord), dimnames = list(ord, ord))
k <- hf$s %in% ord & hf$j %in% ord
tab <- table(factor(hf$s[k], ord), factor(hf$j[k], ord))
A[] <- tab
heat_titled(A, groups = party[ord], colours = party_col)
title_left(sprintf("House: %d members, sponsor (row) by cosponsor (column)", length(ord)),
           "ordered by party, then state; darker: more bills of the row member cosponsored by the column member; lines: party boundary")
```

Two dense blocks lie on the diagonal: the members of each party cosponsor each
other's bills. Within each block, small squares along the diagonal are state
delegations, which cosponsor each other more than the rest of their party does.

## Who gathers cosponsors

```{r sizes, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, fig.alt = "Distribution of the number of cosponsors per bill by sponsor party, House and Senate"}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.4, 3, 1))
for (ch in c("House", "Senate")) {
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, log1p(max(size[chamber == ch]))), ylim = c(0, 1), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  at <- c(0, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300); at <- at[at <= max(size[chamber == ch])]
  axis(1, at = log1p(at), labels = at, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
  abline(h = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), col = rule, lwd = 0.8)
  for (p in c("D", "R")) {
    s <- log1p(size[chamber == ch & party[sponsor] == p])
    e <- stats::ecdf(s); xs <- sort(unique(s))
    lines(c(0, xs), c(0, e(xs)), type = "s", col = party_col[p], lwd = 2.2)
    md <- median(expm1(s))
    text(log1p(md), 0.5, sprintf("median %g", md), pos = if (p == "D") 4 else 2, cex = 0.62, col = party_col[p])
  }
  mtext("cosponsors per bill (log scale)", side = 1, line = 2.2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft)
  mtext("share of bills with at most this many", side = 2, line = 2.6, cex = 0.72, col = ink_soft)
  title_left(ch)
}
legend("bottomright", legend = party_name[c("D", "R")], col = party_col[c("D", "R")], lwd = 2.2, bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
par(op)
```

```{r size-numbers, include = FALSE}
zero <- tapply(size == 0, list(chamber, party[sponsor]), mean)
```

Each curve is the share of a party's bills with at most a given number of
cosponsors. In the House, `r pct(zero["House", "D"])` of Democratic bills and
`r pct(zero["House", "R"])` of Republican bills have no cosponsor at all.

## A hyperevent model of cosponsorship

The model asks which cosponsor sets a sponsor's bill attracts. For each bill
the observed cosponsor set is compared with three control sets that keep the
sponsor and the number of cosponsors and draw the cosponsors at random from the
members of the same chamber (a sender- and size-matched case-control design;
amorem does not yet sample hyperevent controls, so they are drawn here). Every
statistic is computed from the bills introduced strictly before the bill's day:

- **repetition**: past bills of this sponsor that each cosponsor joined,
  averaged over the cosponsors, `hyperedge_subrep(rho = 1, l = 1)` on the
  sponsor's bills;
- **reciprocity**: past bills of each cosponsor that the sponsor joined,
  averaged, `hyperedge_activity(I = cosponsor, J = sponsor)`;
- **cosponsor activity**: past cosponsorships of each cosponsor, averaged;
- **co-cosponsorship**: past bills on which each pair of the cosponsors signed
  together, averaged over pairs (`hyperedge_subrep(rho = 2)` on the
  cosponsor sets);
- **same party** and **same state**: the share of cosponsors from the
  sponsor's party and state.

Counts enter as `log(1 + count)`.

```{r sample}
eligible <- which(size >= 2 & size <= 40 & cb$time >= 60)
set.seed(118)
smp <- sort(sample(eligible, 2500))
c(eligible_bills = length(eligible), sampled = length(smp))
```

The model uses bills with 2 to 40 cosponsors introduced from the 61st day on
(so that every bill has two months of history), and a random sample of
`r fmt(length(smp))` of the `r fmt(length(eligible))` such bills; the
statistics of every sampled bill are computed from all earlier bills.

```{r statistics}
N <- nrow(cb)
by_sponsor <- split(seq_len(N), sponsor)
by_cosponsor <- split(rep(seq_len(N), size), unlist(cb$J))
logs_sponsor <- lapply(by_sponsor, function(i) cb[i, c("I", "J", "time")])
pool <- lapply(c(House = "House", Senate = "Senate"), function(ch)
  sort(unique(c(sponsor[chamber == ch], unlist(cb$J[chamber == ch])))))

hstats <- function(s, J, t) {
  prior_with <- function(j) { i <- by_cosponsor[[j]]; if (is.null(i)) integer(0) else i[cb$time[i] < t] }
  # pairs of J that signed a past bill together: sum over past bills of choose(shared, 2)
  shared <- tabulate(unlist(lapply(J, prior_with)), N)
  c(repetition  = if (is.null(logs_sponsor[[s]])) 0 else
                    hyperedge_subrep(logs_sponsor[[s]], I = s, J = J, t = t, rho = 1, l = 1),
    reciprocity = mean(vapply(J, function(j) if (is.null(logs_sponsor[[j]])) 0 else
                    hyperedge_activity(logs_sponsor[[j]], I = j, J = s, t = t), 0)),
    activity    = mean(vapply(J, function(j) length(prior_with(j)), 0)),
    copair      = sum(choose(shared, 2)) / choose(length(J), 2),
    same_party  = mean(party[J] == party[s], na.rm = TRUE),
    same_state  = mean(state[J] == state[s], na.rm = TRUE))
}

cc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(smp), function(k) {
  i <- smp[k]; s <- sponsor[i]; J <- cb$J[[i]]; t <- cb$time[i]
  others <- setdiff(pool[[chamber[i]]], s)
  rows <- rbind(hstats(s, J, t), t(replicate(3, hstats(s, sample(others, length(J)), t))))
  data.frame(stratum = k, event = c(1L, 0L, 0L, 0L), time = t, rows)
}))
for (v in c("repetition", "reciprocity", "activity", "copair"))
  cc[[paste0("log_", v)]] <- log1p(cc[[v]])
nrow(cc)
```

The co-cosponsorship column uses the identity that the average over all pairs
of `J` of the number of past bills containing the pair equals the sum, over
past bills, of the number of pairs of `J` they contain, divided by the number
of pairs. On a few rows it matches `hyperedge_subrep()` with `rho = 2` exactly:

```{r check-copair}
ulog <- hyperedge_log(I = lapply(cb$J, function(x) if (length(x)) x else "-"),
                      J = replicate(N, character(0), simplify = FALSE), time = cb$time)
chk <- vapply(smp[1:5], function(i) c(
  identity = hstats(sponsor[i], cb$J[[i]], cb$time[i])[["copair"]],
  hyperedge_subrep = hyperedge_subrep(ulog, I = cb$J[[i]], t = cb$time[i], rho = 2, l = 0)), numeric(2))
round(chk, 4)
```

```{r fit}
fit <- rem(event ~ log_repetition + log_reciprocity + log_activity + log_copair +
             same_party + same_state,
           data = cc, method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")
est <- coef(fit)
se <- sqrt(diag(stats::vcov(fit$fit)))
round(cbind(estimate = est, se = se), 3)
```

```{r forest, fig.width = 8.6, fig.height = 4, fig.alt = "Estimated effects with 95 percent intervals"}
labels <- c(log_repetition = "repetition: cosponsored this sponsor before",
            log_reciprocity = "reciprocity: sponsor cosponsored them before",
            log_activity = "cosponsor activity",
            log_copair = "co-cosponsorship of the set",
            same_party = "share from the sponsor's party",
            same_state = "share from the sponsor's state")
forest_titled(est, se, labels = labels[names(est)], col = pal[1])
title_left("Which cosponsor sets a bill attracts", "conditional logit, 3 sender- and size-matched controls per bill; 95% intervals")
```

```{r fit-numbers, include = FALSE}
or <- function(v, d = 1) exp(est[[v]] * d)
```

All six effects are estimated jointly. A cosponsor set entirely from the
sponsor's party, against one with none, multiplies the rate of the bill by
`r fmt(or("same_party"), 1)`; one unit more of `log(1 + repetition)`
multiplies it by `r fmt(or("log_repetition"), 2)`, and one unit more of
co-cosponsorship by `r fmt(or("log_copair"), 2)`. The co-cosponsorship effect
is a hyperedge effect: it measures whether the cosponsors have signed together
before, which no statistic of single sponsor–cosponsor pairs captures.

## Does party homophily change over the two years?

A time-varying effect `tv(same_party)` lets the weight of party vary with the
bill's date. The `gam` backend uses one control per bill:

```{r tv}
w <- widen_case_control(cc[, c("stratum", "event", "log_repetition", "log_reciprocity",
                                "log_activity", "log_copair", "same_party", "same_state")],
                        control_index = 1)
w$time <- cc$time[cc$event == 1][match(w$stratum, unique(cc$stratum))]
fit_tv <- rem(~ log_repetition + log_reciprocity + log_activity + log_copair +
                same_state + tv(same_party, k = 6),
              data = w, method = "gam", time = "time")
summary(fit_tv)$s.table
```

```{r tv-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.4, fig.alt = "Effect of the same-party share over the 118th Congress"}
d <- smooth_data(fit_tv$fit, 1)
d$x <- as.Date("2023-01-03") + d$x
op <- par(mar = c(3.6, 4.2, 3, 1))
plot(d$x, d$fit, type = "n", ylim = range(d$fit - 1.96 * d$se, d$fit + 1.96 * d$se, 0),
     axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2)
polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)), c(d$fit - 1.96 * d$se, rev(d$fit + 1.96 * d$se)), col = alpha(pal[1], 0.18), border = NA)
lines(d$x, d$fit, col = pal[1], lwd = 2.2)
axis.Date(1, at = seq(as.Date("2023-03-01"), as.Date("2025-01-01"), by = "3 months"), format = "%b %Y",
          tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft)
axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)
mtext("change in log-rate, all vs no cosponsors\nfrom the sponsor's party", side = 2, line = 2.2, cex = 0.68, col = ink_soft)
rug(as.Date("2023-01-03") + w$time, col = alpha(ink_soft, 0.15), ticksize = 0.02)
text(min(d$x), par("usr")[3], "each tick below: one sampled bill", adj = c(0, -2.2), cex = 0.62, col = ink_soft)
title_left("Party homophily over the 118th Congress", "tv(same_party): change in the log-rate when all cosponsors, rather than none, share the sponsor's party; 95% band")
par(op)
```

```{r anim, echo = FALSE}
d0 <- as.Date("2023-01-03")
brk <- seq(0, as.numeric(as.Date("2025-01-04") - d0) + 14, by = 14)
win_lab <- format(d0 + head(brk, -1), "%d %b %Y")
caucus <- ifelse(party == "R", "R", "D")          # the independents caucus with the Democrats
sen <- flows$ch == "Senate"
t_sen <- rep(cb$time, size)[sen]
cross_sen <- caucus[flows$s[sen]] != caucus[flows$j[sen]]
sen_bridge <- tapply(cross_sen, flows$j[sen], mean, na.rm = TRUE)
sen_n <- table(flows$j[sen])
lab_ids <- names(sort(sen_bridge[names(sen_n)[sen_n >= 50]], decreasing = TRUE))[1:3]
anim_events(flows$s[sen], flows$j[sen], t_sen, brk, win_lab,
            node_col = setNames(party_col[caucus], names(caucus)),
            n_nodes = 95, node_label = short[lab_ids],
            title = "Senate cosponsorship, two weeks at a time",
            sub = "95 most active senators; blue: Democratic caucus, pink: Republicans; grey line: across caucuses; faint: previous 3 windows",
            fps = 4, alt = "Animation of the Senate cosponsorship network in two-week windows over the 118th Congress")
```

```{r anim-numbers, include = FALSE}
wf <- findInterval(t_sen, brk)
xw <- tapply(cross_sen, wf, mean, na.rm = TRUE)
nw <- tabulate(wf, length(brk) - 1)
xw <- xw[as.integer(names(xw)) %in% which(nw >= 100)]
```

Each frame is a two-week window of Senate bills, and the bar strip under it
marks the window in the whole record. The labelled senators are the three
(among those with at least 50 cosponsorships) whose cosponsorships most often
go to the other caucus. Over the fortnights with at least 100 Senate
cosponsorships, the share that crosses caucus lines ranges from
`r pct(min(xw))` (fortnight from `r win_lab[as.integer(names(which.min(xw)))]`)
to `r pct(max(xw))` (fortnight from `r win_lab[as.integer(names(which.max(xw)))]`).

```{r tv-numbers, include = FALSE}
q <- function(dd) d$fit[which.min(abs(as.numeric(d$x - as.Date(dd))))]
```

The curve is the weight of the same-party share at each date, holding the
other statistics fixed: `r fmt(q("2023-06-01"), 2)` in June 2023 and
`r fmt(q("2024-09-01"), 2)` in September 2024. `summary(fit_tv)$s.table` tests
whether it departs from a constant.

## Where to go from here

- Match controls on the sponsor's party as well as the sponsor, so that the
  same-party effect compares sets the sponsor could plausibly recruit.
- Add `nl()` effects of the statistics, as in
  [Hyperedge models](hyperedge-models.html), to test whether repetition
  saturates.
- Fit the House and the Senate separately: the Senate has 100 members and a
  denser cosponsorship network.
